primary_responsibilities: Developing comprehensive media strategies and channel mix recommendations aligned to client or brand objectives, target audiences, budgets, and campaign timelines
Building and maintaining media flowcharts and detailed media plans (documenting placements, flight dates, budgets, CPMs, impressions, and estimated reach/frequency)
Conducting audience research using syndicated data tools to understand target consumer media consumption and behavior
Evaluating publisher and platform proposals, writing POVs (point-of-view documents) on new channels, formats, and opportunities
Collaborating with buying teams to ensure planned strategies are executable at planned CPMs and that contracted delivery matches plan
Monitoring campaign performance against plan, reconciling budget pacing, and recommending optimizations
daily_tasks: Updating media flowcharts and budget trackers in Excel or planning platforms as campaign details change
Reviewing overnight performance data from platforms (Google Ads, Meta, DSP dashboards) and flagging pacing issues or underdelivery
Responding to internal briefs and client requests for scenario planning, budget reallocation, or new channel recommendations
Meeting with media sales representatives to review new programs, opportunities, or research supporting their inventory
Writing and updating campaign documentation: insertion orders, client approval memos, POVs, competitive landscape summaries
Coordinating with creative and trafficking teams on ad specifications, tagging, and deadline management
tools_they_use: Media planning and flowchart software (Lumanu, MediaLink, Bionic Advertising Systems, or custom Excel/Google Sheets templates)
Audience research and syndicated data platforms (MRI-Simmons, GWI, Nielsen National TV, Comscore for digital)
Competitive intelligence platforms (Kantar Ad Intelligence, MediaRadar, Pathmatics/Sensor Tower)
Digital platform dashboards for monitoring (Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, The Trade Desk, DV360)
Project management and workflow tools (Workfront, Asana, Jira for trafficking and campaign coordination)
Presentation tools (PowerPoint, Google Slides for client-facing plan presentations)
context.content_needs: Media planners benefit most from templates, calculators, and how-to frameworks rather than thought leadership. High-value content includes: channel comparison matrices (CPM benchmarks, reach, targeting capabilities), audience research guides, media math reference sheets (GRP/reach/frequency calculations), briefing templates, RFP templates, flowchart and media plan templates, CPM benchmark reports by channel, and decision frameworks for channel selection based on objectives.
decision_criteria: Audience reach and composition: Does the channel deliver sufficient reach against the target audience at a meaningful index?
Cost efficiency: What is the CPM or CPC versus alternatives, and what is the cost per target impression (CPTI)?
Channel fit to objective: Does the channel's format and context support the campaign objective (awareness, consideration, conversion)?
Attribution and measurability: Can the channel's contribution to outcomes be tracked and reported to clients?
Competitive landscape: Are competitors present in this channel, and does the brand need to defend or differentiate in this space?
Budget scalability: Can the plan be executed at the approved budget, or are minimum investment thresholds a barrier?
pain_points: Spending an excessive proportion of time on administrative tasks—building, updating, and reformatting media plan spreadsheets and flowcharts—rather than strategic thinking
Difficulty getting real-time budget pacing visibility across multiple platforms and partners without manually pulling reports and reconciling in Excel
Being handed a brief with insufficient information (no defined target audience, vague objectives, unrealistic budget for stated goals) and being expected to produce a plan immediately
Keeping CPM benchmarks and channel data current—reference data ages quickly and outdated benchmarks undermine credibility with clients
Coordinating deliverables across multiple internal teams (creative, strategy, analytics, buying) and external partners while managing competing deadlines
Justifying media mix decisions to clients who have preconceived channel preferences not supported by data or audience research
context.career_path: Assistant Media Planner → Media Planner → Senior Media Planner → Associate Media Director → Media Director → VP, Media / Group Media Director → Managing Director, Media. At agencies, this path typically takes 7–12 years from entry-level to Director. In-house brand roles often offer accelerated progression with broader responsibilities. Some planners specialize into channel strategy (digital-only, TV specialty) rather than following the generalist management track.
context.reports_to: Associate Media Director or Media Director (at agencies); Head of Media or CMO (at in-house brands); Group Account Director (in integrated agency structures where media planning is embedded in account teams)
collaborates_with: Media Buyers / Investment team (executes the channels the planner recommends and negotiates rates)
Analytics / Measurement team (defines KPIs, attribution methodology, and interprets performance data)
Account Managers / Client Leads (the interface between planner's recommendations and client approval)
Creative Strategy and Creative teams (ensures channel-specific ad specifications are met and creative is adapted for placement contexts)
Brand / Marketing Strategy team (aligns media strategy to overall brand and campaign objectives)
context.format_preferences: Templates and calculators above all else—media planners are highly pragmatic and value tools that reduce time-on-task. Flowchart templates, RFP templates, and brief templates are high-utility. Concise channel fact sheets (one-pagers) for client education. Benchmarking guides with current CPM ranges by channel. How-to guides for newer channels or formats. Avoid long-form thought leadership articles; prioritize scannable formats with clear data tables.
